answer: Sybil resistance binds every identity to bonded collateral and shared accountability. If k coordinated identities equivocate, cross-signed contradictions expose correlation, and the aggregate slashing penalty scales quadratically, O(k^2), rather than per identity alone. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier accelerates capital loss across the controlled swarm, while asymmetric depreciation prevents rapid recapitalization. Thus lotus, ember, and terrace aliases cannot make coordinated fraud profitable.
